chunks: P-type vs N-type semiconductors. The question: What is the difference between P-type semiconductors vs N-type semiconductors?
N-type and P-type are two flavors of silicon, made by adding a tiny amount of a different element on purpose. N-type has extra free electrons.
P-type has a shortage of electrons, which creates holes that act like moving positive charges. Neither flavor is charged overall.
The difference is only which carrier is plentiful.
Picture a theater where every seat is taken. For N-type, a few extra people stand in the aisles, and they can move around freely. For P-type, a few seats are empty.
People next to an empty seat slide over, and the empty seat appears to move the other way. The standing people are electrons, and the empty seats are holes.
The analogy fails in one way: holes are not real objects, only the absence of an electron.
In the N-type lattice the phosphorus atom has one valence electron that no bond needs, so it wanders off as a free electron and leaves a fixed P⁺ ion.
In the P-type lattice the boron atom is one electron short; an incomplete bond (the open red circle) can be filled by a neighbour, so the hole moves while the B⁻ ion stays put.
Dopant: the impurity atom added on purpose to change the silicon. Majority carrier: the carrier type that is plentiful. Minority carrier: the carrier type that is scarce.
Hole: an empty electron spot that moves like a positive charge. Valence electrons: the outer electrons that form bonds. Silicon has four.
Add phosphorus, which has five valence electrons, to silicon. Four bond with neighbors and the fifth is free. That is N-type.
Add boron, which has three, and one bond is missing an electron. That is P-type.
With 10 to the 16 phosphorus atoms in each cubic centimeter, there are about 10 to the 16 free electrons there and only about 10 to the 4 holes. That is the whole idea.
"N-type and P-type are silicon doped on purpose so one carrier dominates.
N-type uses a donor like phosphorus with five valence electrons, so the extra electron is free and electrons are the majority carrier.
P-type uses an acceptor like boron with three valence electrons, which leaves a missing electron, a hole, that behaves like a mobile positive charge.
Both are electrically neutral. The minority carrier is set by np equals n i squared . Joining a P and an N region makes a PN junction, the basis of diodes and transistors."
